props.name: caveats

props.name: uniaxial

Earlier calculations found elastic instability

props.name: open-question:label
props.text: Open question

props.name: open-question
props.text:
Which instability occurs first for a generic
state of tension?

props.name: study:label
props.text: This study

props.name: study
props.text:
Compare the elastic limit with a finite-wave-
vector K1 phonon instability.

The paper opens with two findings from different loading contexts: nearly ideal nanoindentation caused failure, while previous armchair/zigzag phonon calculations identified elastic instability. The authors ask which instability comes first for a generic tensile state. This comparison motivates the calculations; it does not claim that the experiment and calculations reproduce identical boundary conditions.

props.name: figure-1
props.alt: figure-1: In-plane phonon dispersion branches for unstrained and strained graphene, showing softening toward K1 instability.

props.name: figure-1:caption
props.text:
Fig. 1. In-plane phonon branches under equibiaxial strain;
the K1 mode approaches instability at K.

Figure 1 shows significant softening of in-plane phonons under equibiaxial strain. The phonon calculation places the K1 soft mode at ε_A = 0.205–0.212. A separate mode-energy analysis predicts ε_A = 0.213. These are closely matching calculated thresholds, not a direct measurement of breaking strain.

props.name: strength:label

props.name: strength
props.text:
The K-cell stress drops near softening; the

props.name: figure-1
props.alt: figure-1: Nominal stress curves under equibiaxial strain, with a stress drop near the K1 soft-mode onset.

props.name: figure-1:caption
props.text:
Fig. 3. Nominal stress versus equibiaxial strain; the
K-cell response drops near K1 softening.

The paper reports that further strain deepens and widens the K1 double-well potential. It interprets the mode as a route toward isolated hexagonal rings and reduced strength. Figure 3 supplies the mechanical response: the K-cell stress curve drops near the K1 softening. Present the structural pathway as the authors’ interpretation, not as a directly imaged transition in this calculation.

props.name: elastic-regions

props.name: k1-region:label
props.text: Region II

props.name: k1-region
props.text:
The K1-mode instability arrives first; the

props.name: figure-1
props.alt: figure-1: Failure-mode map separating elastic-instability and K1-instability regions across tensile directions.

props.name: figure-1:caption
props.text:
Fig. 4(a). Maximum stable strain across tensile directions; regions I/
III are elastic-limited and region II is K1-limited.

The authors identify regions I and III as elastic-instability failure, where the elastic limit precedes the K1 mode. The complementary region is limited first by the K1 instability. They emphasize that equibiaxial loading follows a different route from the usual uniaxial armchair/zigzag case. Use the labels in Figure 4(a) when presenting the regions.

props.name: shear-scope
props.text:

props.name: figure-1
props.alt: figure-1: Failure map after a 15-degree rotation of the coordinate system.

props.name: figure-1:caption
props.text:
Fig. 4(c). At 15° rotation, the failure map remains
within the original/rotated envelope.

The coordinates were rotated in 3-degree increments; Figure 4(c) displays the 15-degree case. The rotated results remain within the envelope formed by the original and 15-degree curves. The authors report no qualitative shear-induced change and only small quantitative shifts to K1 onset. Because graphene is anisotropic, the paper notes that the orientation/shear enumeration is not exhaustive.

props.name: alternatives

Lee et al. report a nominal equibiaxial breaking strain of 0.225. The paper says this is in much better agreement with its calculated equibiaxial elastic-instability strain of 0.216. The authors suggest that K1 may be stabilized in nanoindentation, but they do not establish this. They identify possible differences involving the indenter environment and the experimental versus constructed equibiaxial strain state.

props.name: figure-1
props.alt: figure-1: Summary of elastic-limited and K1-limited failure regions across tensile directions.

props.name: figure-1:caption
props.text:
Fig. 4(a). The loading-direction map summarizes where elastic and
K1-mode instabilities occur first.

The paper’s central result is mode selection by tensile state: elastic instability in regions I/III and a K1 soft-mode route in region II. The authors connect K1 softening with a phase transition and reduced strength in some states. The nanoindentation comparison does not settle which route occurred. The paper says its orientation/shear treatment is incomplete. PaperWorkflow’s synthesis readiness also marks evidence coverage as review, so this deck should not be read as exhaustive coverage of all workflow facets.
